prompt: Build a countdown string like "3 2 1 go" using recursion, where n = 0 gives just "go". Complete the countdown method, then run the tests.
explanation: The recursive picture: countdown(3) is just "3 " glued onto countdown(2), which is "2 " glued onto countdown(1), and so on until the base case countdown(0) supplies "go". Each call handles one number and delegates the rest to a smaller version of the same problem. Because the base case provides the final word, no call needs to worry about trailing spaces.
hints: Base case: when n is 0, return exactly "go" -- no numbers, no spaces.
Recursive case: the result is n, a space, then whatever countdown(n - 1) returns.
n + " " + countdown(n - 1) does the string building; the base case guarantees the string always ends in "go".
